text:
Alex K: Quick q — we keep circling the 'smart-mux' gateway idea. My rough pitch: one edge that detects client protocol (grpc/json), does minimal proto<->json translation for legacy clients, enforces routing-policy header, and emits unified telemetry. Pros: single place for quota/routing/telemetry. Cons: more logic at the edge, CPU + complexity. Thoughts?

Maria P: I lean towards a slim shim that errors for unsupported clients and points them to the proper SDK. Simpler surface area, fewer weird translation footguns. But yeah, >1 teams will complain about migrating. :grimacing:

Samir R: Smart-mux advantage — we can canonicalize requests before they hit the runtime. That lets us have a single set of metrics and a single quota check path. Also easier to do sampling and golden prompt checks.

Jen T: Biggest product risk is billing/units. JSON expansions could change token counts. If we translate at the edge, do we charge on pre-translation or post-translation size? Need a clear decision for the console and billing pipelines.

Pat S: Hybrid idea: thin edge (fast paths) + optional translator sidecar for tenants that need it. Keeps P95 low for modern clients, lets legacy customers opt-in. Might complicate routing policies though.

Alex K: Benchmarks I ran on a prototype smart-mux (Go service + Proto->JSON translator) — added ~6-9ms p95 on small requests; bigger generative loads dominated by model time so relative cost small. But it did increase CPU on the edge pool by ~18%.

Samir R: If we centralize translation we can add deterministic canonicalization so our quality evals are consistent. Also easier to attach per-route QA checks.

Maria P: I'm worried about subtle semantic mismatches (enums, unknown fields, repeated field ordering) — translator might silently change behavior. That will generate hard-to-debug regressions for clients.

Jen T: Operationally, we need console signals: flow-level telemetry (orig proto vs translated), translation error rate, translation latency, and delta between token counts pre/post. Rollout UX: feature flag per-tenant + canary dashboard with those metrics.

Pat S: Could we implement translation as an isolated binary that we can hot-swap? So if we see regressions we can rollback the translator without touching the rest of the edge.

Alex K: Short config sketch for a routing policy header idea:

```yaml
- match: 
    header: x-client-protocol
    values: [grpc, json]
  action: route
    pool: runtime-v2
  transform: smart-mux (optional)
```

Samir R: We'll also need quota headers propagated through translations. My suggestion: set X-Quota-Units based on canonical model token estimate at translation time and use that for billing/console attribution.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for branch smart-mux-edge -> env:staging, canary=3% :rocket:

Maria P: If we do quota units at translation time we have to ensure determinism. Otherwise customers will get inconsistent billing. Maybe we treat translation-changed tokens as 'billed at runtime' to be safe.

Jen T: Proposed rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged translator behind alpha tenants, 2) 3% canary with canary dashboard (translation_error_rate, delta_tokens, p95_latency, 5xx_rate), 3) 25% if no regressions, 4) tenant opt-in for legacy support. If regressions appear we rollback translator binary.

Pat S: Agree — also add a console toggle to 'show pre-translation payload' for 48h after rollout so SEs can inspect mismatches.

Alex K: Who wants to own the initial POC? I can do the translator service prototype; need someone on telemetry/dashboard to add the canary panels.

Samir R: I can wire the metrics and sampling traces. Will add a golden-prompt check and a small eval hook to alert on quality regressions.

Jen T: I'll write the rollout playbook and the billing question doc (do we bill pre/post). Want to include rollback triggers: translation_error_rate > 0.5% OR p95 increased by >10ms OR delta_tokens > 15% for top-10 routes.

Maria P: If we follow that conservative plan I'm OK to try the POC but we should explicitly document translator semantic guarantees and add end-to-end integration tests.

Alex K: Great. I'll open a small RFC + repo (link: https://go/rdw-smart-mux) and start the POC. Samir/Jen thanks for volunteering. Pat/Maria please add privacy/semantics concerns to the RFC.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary health check passed (3/3), metrics flowing to canary dashboard.

Jen T: Sweet. We'll reconvene after the first canary run. TL;DR: experiment smart-mux behind flags, telemetries + billing decisions first, rollback conditions defined. :thumbsup:
